newsitem.title: AZERBAIJAN: Russia's LUKoil, Azeris, sign deal on oil reserves.
newsitem.headline: Russia's LUKoil, Azeris, sign deal on oil reserves.

text.p: Russian oil giant LUKoil and the State Oil Company of Azerbaijan (SOCAR) signed a memorandum on Wednesday to begin talks on jointly exploring and developing the Yalama oil field in the Caspian Sea, LUkoil President Vagit Alekperov said.

Alekperov told reporters outside SOCAR headquarters that the field, about 25 km (15 miles) wide and 30 km (20 miles) long and straddling the Azeri and Russian sectors of the Caspian, could contain up to 50 million tonnes of crude.

"It is difficult to say (about reserves) because there are no geophysical details or wells there, but according to our estimates we think there could be up to 50 million in obtainable reserves," he said.
LUKoil has a stake in three other joint projects with SOCAR to develop offshore Caspian fields.
Similar memorandums in the past between SOCAR and foreign oil companies have led to the signing of fully-fledged drilling and production-sharing contacts.
Alekperov said that under the memorandum, a 90-day negotiating period to draw up a formal production sharing agreement between SOCAR and LUKoil would commence.
He gave no estimate of the possible investment in exploring or developing the field.

He said negotiations were continuing with SOCAR on joint development of the Inam offshore Caspian field, about 120 km southeast of the capital Baku and estimated by the Azeris to contain about 200 million tonnes of crude oil.
